sections.heading: Section 1: Null & Alternative Hypotheses, Type I & Type II Errors

questions.q: Define a Type I error in hypothesis testing.
choices: Failing to reject $H_0$ when $H_0$ is false
Setting the significance level too high
questions.answer: A Type I error occurs when a true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected. The probability of a Type I error equals the significance level $\alpha$.

questions.q: Define a Type II error in hypothesis testing.
choices: Failing to reject $H_0$ when $H_0$ is false
questions.answer: A Type II error (probability $\beta$) occurs when the test fails to reject a false null hypothesis.

questions.q: A machine produces metal pins with mean length 5.0 cm. A technician suspects the machine is out of adjustment and producing pins of different mean length. What are the appropriate hypotheses?
questions.answer: A non-directional suspicion ('different mean length') requires a two-tailed alternative hypothesis $H_1: \mu \neq 5.0$.

sections.heading: Section 2: Testing Population Mean with Normal Distribution

questions.q: A test of $H_0: \mu = 80$ against $H_1: \mu > 80$ at the $5\%$ level is conducted. A sample of $n = 36$ from $N(\mu, 144)$ gives $\bar{x} = 83.5$. What is the value of the test statistic $z$?
For the test in the previous question ($z = 1.75$), what is the test conclusion at the $5\%$ significance level (critical value $1.645$)?
choices: Reject $H_0$; there is sufficient evidence that the mean is greater than 80
Accept $H_0$; the difference is due to chance
questions.answer: Since $z = 1.75 > 1.645$, the test statistic falls in the critical region. Reject $H_0$ at the 5% level.

questions.q: What is the $p$-value for the test statistic $z = 1.75$ in a one-tailed test?

sections.heading: Section 3: Testing Parameters with Poisson & Binomial Models

questions.q: A company claims its weekly defect rate is $\lambda = 2$. In a given week, 6 defects are observed. Test $H_0: \lambda = 2$ against $H_1: \lambda > 2$ by calculating $P(X \geq 6)$ under $H_0$.
At the $5\%$ significance level, what is the conclusion for the defect test in the previous question ($p = 0.0166$)?
choices: Reject $H_0$; the defect rate has significantly increased

questions.q: A seed packet claims a $90\%$ germination rate. A gardener tests 20 seeds and finds 15 germinate. To test $H_0: p = 0.9$ against $H_1: p < 0.9$, which probability must be computed?
questions.answer: For a lower-tail test ($H_1: p < 0.9$), the $p$-value is the probability of observing an outcome as extreme as or more extreme than the observed value: $P(X \leq 15)$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Critical Regions & Power of a Test

questions.q: For a test of $H_0: \mu = 50$ vs $H_1: \mu < 50$ using $n = 25, \sigma = 10$, find the critical value for $\bar{x}$ at the $5\%$ level ($z_c = -1.645$).
In the previous test (critical region $\bar{X} < 46.71$), what is the probability of a Type II error if the true mean is $\mu = 45$?
What is the statistical power of the test in the previous question (where $\beta = 0.1964$)?
questions.answer: Power of a test is defined as $1 - \beta = 1 - 0.1964 = 0.8036$ (or $80.36\%$).
